pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these solids can be poured? (1 mark)
   A. Stone
   B. Flour
   C. Brick
   D. Ruler

2. Which of these is a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Air in a football
   C. Chalk
   D. Sugar

3. Which of these do we measure using litres? (1 mark)
   A. Mass of a book
   B. Volume of juice
   C. Time of a race
   D. Length of a rope

4. Which of these is a reason we need gases? (1 mark)
   A. We can sit on them
   B. We can write with them
   C. We can build houses with them
   D. We breathe air

5. A bag has 1 kg of rice and 250 g of beans. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 1025 g
   B. 350 g
   C. 2500 g
   D. 1250 g

6. Which is the best way to manage the food remains from the school kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Bury plastic with them
   B. Throw them in a river
   C. Burn them near classrooms
   D. Put them in a compost pit

7. Which item is a paper waste that can be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bottle
   B. Banana peel
   C. Old newspapers
   D. Glass bottle

8. At a wedding, what can organisers do to keep the place clean? (1 mark)
   A. Throw waste in a river
   B. Leave waste on the ground
   C. Burn plastic
   D. Provide bins and clean after the event

9. Which is an example of recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Buying less food
   B. Throwing paper in a bin
   C. Using a tin for a pencil holder
   D. Melting scrap metal to make new items

10. Which of these is e-waste? (1 mark)
   A. An old phone
   B. A banana peel
   C. A leaf
   D. A paper bag

11. In a school, who could check that bins are emptied and clean? (1 mark)
   A. Class monitors
   B. Only the visitors
   C. Nobody
   D. Only the wind

12. What should you wear when collecting waste? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. A hat only
   C. Gloves and closed shoes
   D. Sandals only

13. What is a good use of old clothes? (1 mark)
   A. Bury them in a garden pit
   B. Use them as cleaning cloths
   C. Throw them in a drain
   D. Burn them near a house

14. Which of these makes a good compost mixture? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetable peelings, dry leaves and some soil
   B. Glass and metal
   C. Plastic and tins
   D. Batteries and plastic

15. Which of these is a source of dirty water we should not drink? (1 mark)
   A. Water used to wash clothes
   B. Clean tap water
   C. Boiled and treated water
   D. Safe borehole water

16. What does water conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Boiling water
   B. Wasting water
   C. Selling water
   D. Using water carefully and protecting water sources

17. Which of these is a way of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving a tap running
   B. Fixing leaks
   C. Using a bucket
   D. Closing taps

18. Which of these is a source of fresh water? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A puddle of sea water
   C. The sea
   D. A salty lake only

19. Why do we need water for farming? (1 mark)
   A. To bake bricks only
   B. Crops and livestock need water
   C. To make wind
   D. To make stones

20. Which reused water is safe for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Water that washed vegetables
   B. Water that washed a car
   C. None of the used washing water
   D. Water that washed clothes

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how you would make a dustbin from locally available materials. (4 marks)

22. A jug holds 500 ml of water. Musa pours in 250 ml and later takes out 100 ml. How much water is in the jug at the end? (4 marks)

23. Explain why burning waste is not a good way of managing waste and give better methods. (5 marks)

24. A pupil says that empty containers have nothing inside. Explain why the pupil is wrong and how you would show it. (5 marks)

25. Describe how you would measure 300 ml of water using a measuring jug, and how you would measure the mass of a mango. (5 marks)

26. Explain why sand is not a liquid although it can be poured. (3 marks)

27. State two dangers of leaving waste in the environment. (2 marks)

28. A tap leaks 4 litres every hour. How much water is lost in 6 hours? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Flour
   Flour is made of tiny solid grains that can pour.

2. A — Cooking oil
   Cooking oil flows and takes the shape of its container.

3. B — Volume of juice
   Litres measure volume.

4. D — We breathe air
   Air gives us oxygen for breathing.

5. D — 1250 g
   1 kg = 1000 g, and 1000 + 250 = 1250 g.

6. D — Put them in a compost pit
   Kitchen waste can be composted.

7. C — Old newspapers
   Paper can be turned into new paper.

8. D — Provide bins and clean after the event
   Bins and cleaning keep the place tidy.

9. D — Melting scrap metal to make new items
   Melting metal to make new items is recycling.

10. A — An old phone
   E-waste means old electrical and electronic items.

11. A — Class monitors
   Monitors can share the responsibility.

12. C — Gloves and closed shoes
   Gloves and shoes protect from cuts and germs.

13. B — Use them as cleaning cloths
   Reusing old cloth as cleaning cloths reduces waste.

14. A — Vegetable peelings, dry leaves and some soil
   Composting uses natural plant waste.

15. A — Water used to wash clothes
   Used washing water is dirty and unsafe.

16. D — Using water carefully and protecting water sources
   Conservation means saving water and using it wisely.

17. A — Leaving a tap running
   A running tap that is not in use wastes water.

18. A — A river
   Rivers carry fresh water that people can use.

19. B — Crops and livestock need water
   Water is needed for plants and animals.

20. C — None of the used washing water
   Used washing water is not safe to drink.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a strong bucket, box or container. Cut and smooth the top and cover any sharp edge. Make a lid if possible. Paint a label saying waste only and put it in a suitable place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 500 + 250 = 750, 1 mark for 750 - 100, 1 mark for 650, 1 mark for the unit ml.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Burning gives harmful smoke, especially from plastic. Better: reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and use bins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for better methods.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: They are full of air which is matter. Air takes up space. For example the upside-down cup pushed into water stays dry inside or a balloon swells with air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air is matter, 1 mark for an activity, 1 mark for the observation, 1 mark for the conclusion.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Place the jug on a flat surface, pour water until the level reaches the 300 mark with your eye level with the water. For the mango, place it on a balance and read the mass in grams.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for flat surface, pouring to 300 ml, eye level, using a balance, reading in grams.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each grain of sand is a small solid with its own shape. The grains are piled together and pour as a pile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for grains being solids, 1 mark for grains having shape, 1 mark for conclusion.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Blocked drains and floods, disease from flies and rats, harm to animals, injuries from glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each danger.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: 24 litres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 6 and 1 mark for the answer with units.
